html:
The unified interface for agent harnesses.

Build agent products without handling harness engineering. HarnessRouter is the infrastructure layer that turns existing harnesses like Codex and Claude Code into plug-and-play agent backends, letting your product run tasks, retrieve results, and switch harnesses through one API.

HarnessRouter implements the Unified Harness Protocol (UHP) and provides an OpenAI Responses-compatible API, handling persistent sessions, streaming progress, files, artifacts, cancellation, and structured failures.

Eight harness × model configurations on the same task. Each metric compares its best and worst results. The lowest-cost and fastest configurations vary by task. Methodology

26 harness bases today: Codex, Claude Code, Hermes, Pi, DeepSeek Harness, OpenCode, Kilo Code, Qwen Code, Gemini CLI, Cline, Oh My Pi, goose, Kimi Code CLI, MiniMax Code, Aider, OpenHands, CheetahClaws, Grok Build, Agent Zero, System One, Qoder Cloud Agent, MiMo Code, jcode, OpenSquilla, nanobot and ZeroClaw. The support matrix shows which run on which provider.

Tip

Get started: Run locally · Integrate into your product · Starter kits · Use managed Cloud

Self-host Community Edition with your own provider keys, on infrastructure you control.

Start with one Docker command, wait for the first launch, then connect a model provider and run your first task.

You need: Docker · About 4 GB of disk · A provider API key

No HarnessRouter account required. No bundled model or trial key.

docker run -d --name harnessrouter \
  -p 127.0.0.1:3000:3000 \
  -v harnessrouter:/data \
  harnessrouter/harnessrouter

Docker pulls the image if needed. The named volume preserves your database, files, installed harness CLIs, and workspaces between restarts.

Existing installation or custom setup

Already installed? 

docker pull harnessrouter/harnessrouter
downloads the latest image but does not upgrade a running container. Follow the upgrade and backup guide.

Port 3000 busy? Use 

-p 127.0.0.1:3100:3000
and open port 3100 instead. Keep the loopback binding while using the initial credentials.

Do not add 

--user
. The entrypoint and Runner need root to manage per-session users. The Console and Gateway run unprivileged; agent processes run as their session’s user.

For version pinning, Compose, and scripted setup, see the setup guide.

docker logs -f harnessrouter

The first launch installs the enabled harness CLIs. Continue when the logs show:

      
[harnessrouter] ready on :3000

Press Ctrl+C to stop following logs. The container keeps running.

Console not ready or a harness missing?

If the browser refuses the connection, retry after a few seconds while the Console finishes starting. For a missing harness, check 

backends available:
and any 
requested but not installed
warning in the logs.

Open http://localhost:3000, or your chosen host port, and sign in:

Username 
harnessrouter
Password 
harnessrouter

Warning

Change the default password in Profile. Keep the instance local until you change it. Saving briefly restarts the Console and signs out other browsers.

See the sign-in screen

Using an existing volume or custom credentials? Check credential precedence and setup.

These credentials sign you into the Console. You do not need a HarnessRouter API key to run tasks here.

Open the account menu at the bottom of the rail and choose Bring your own key. Find your provider, press Add key, and paste its API key. Its supported models become available in the Console.

This provider key authorizes model requests. It is separate from the HarnessRouter API key used for product integration below.

See the provider setup screen

Open Start, say what your agent should do for your users, and press Continue. In Set up an agent harness, leave the agent harness and model on Auto or choose them, then save. HarnessRouter builds the setup on one of your own models: it writes the agent's instructions, picks the harness, model, skills, plugins and tools the job needs, and leaves an example request in the box. Send it to run the first task.

Try an example first. Under Start in HarnessRouter, pick one of the three example jobs. Its request plays back a recorded run, so you see a finished task without spending tokens. Write under it to carry on with your own model.

Open the setup in Studio and choose Settings to change its model, instructions, skills, plugins, tools, environment and limits. Add plugins, skills, MCP servers and environments for the whole workspace under Add-ons. The agent harness is fixed once a setup is saved: make a new setup to use another.

See New setup

Run product tasks with built-in or custom harnesses as pluggable agent backends. Call your self-hosted instance’s OpenAI Responses-compatible API and select the harness with 

metadata.harness_id
. No Cloud deployment is required.

Once your harness runs successfully in the Console:

  • Open API Keys in the Console rail of the same CE instance (default local address), name the key, and press Create.
  • Store the secret shown once as 
    HARNESSROUTER_API_KEY
    in your product backend. Never expose it in browser code. This CE-issued key is separate from your Console password and provider key.
  • Call the API with the Harness ID shown in the Console and a model served by your connected provider.
export HARNESSROUTER_BASE_URL=http://localhost:3000/api/harness

curl --fail-with-body -sS "$HARNESSROUTER_BASE_URL/v1/responses" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${HARNESSROUTER_API_KEY:?}" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "input":"Reply with exactly: it works.",
    "metadata":{"harness_id":"codex"},
    "model":"gpt-5.4-mini",
    "stream":false
  }'

The task and its transcript appear in the same workspace in the Console. Set 

"stream": true
to receive server-sent events.

Join a caller's trace to the task.

Send the W3C Trace Context headers 

traceparent
and 
tracestate
on the request, and the task's model calls carry a child of that trace: the same trace id, a new span id and the sampled flag, so the provider's log and yours are one trace. A value that is not valid W3C syntax is dropped, never refused: a broken tracing header does not fail a task. 
baggage
is never read and never leaves the instance.

Retry a task without running it twice.

Send the same request with the same 

Idempotency-Key
when retrying a task. For example, send this request twice using the URL and API key above (key generation needs Python 3):

IDEMPOTENCY_KEY=$(python3 -c 'import uuid; print(uuid.uuid4())')

for attempt in 1 2; do
  curl --fail-with-body -sS "$HARNESSROUTER_BASE_URL/v1/responses" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer ${HARNESSROUTER_API_KEY:?}" \
    -H 'content-type: application/json' \
    -H "Idempotency-Key: $IDEMPOTENCY_KEY" \
    -d '{
      "input":"Reply with exactly: it works.",
      "metadata":{"harness_id":"codex"},
      "model":"gpt-5.4-mini",
      "stream":false
    }'
  printf '\n'
done

Both responses have the same 

id
, and the session contains one turn: the retry returns the first request's result without starting another execution. If the first request is still running, the retry waits for it. Use a new key for each new logical request. Reusing a key with a different request body returns 
409
; changing only 
stream
still counts as the same request. See Tasks §6: Idempotency.

Never put a long exact value such as a token, an id or a hash in the prompt: the agent retypes what it reads, and a model drops and swaps characters in strings like that. Attach it as a file (

POST /v1/files
, then an 
input_file
block; the file lands in the agent's working directory under its filename before every turn that carries it) or hand it to the agent through the harness's environment. A harness takes an 
env
map whose values resolve on every turn: 
$headers.X-Name
takes that header from the request (declare it in 
additional_headers
), 
vault:name
takes a stored secret, anything else is used as written. The agent's shell and tools start with those variables set, so a task can say "the token is in $DEPLOY_TOKEN", and a value that came through a reference is redacted from everything that leaves the sandbox, the response, the stream, the trace and the stored record, even when the agent prints it. A 
vault:
reference reads only a secret your own workspace stored through 
PUT /v1/mcp-secrets/{ref}
. The redaction protects the record, not the agent: a value the agent can read it can also send elsewhere if a prompt or a page tells it to, so hand it a token scoped to the user and the task, short-lived and least privilege.

The whole API is described at 

$HARNESSROUTER_BASE_URL/v1/openapi.json
, generated from the routes, with a browsable copy at 
/v1/docs
.

The default URL works when your backend and CE run on the same computer. From another machine or container, use a reachable URL for the CE instance. Read the complete self-hosted API and networking guide →

Your application can… How
Start tasks Send instructions and check execution status
Continue sessions Send follow-up instructions with 
previous_response_id
Stream progress Receive live updates as the agent works
Work with files Attach input files and retrieve generated outputs
Cancel tasks Stop work that is no longer needed
Inspect execution Review structured errors and execution traces

Power agentic features in your product with agent harnesses, including knowledge-work tasks such as creating content and analyzing data. Explore these ready-to-use kits to see harnesses in action as pluggable backends.

An agent harness turns your brief into slide content and layouts for an editable deck.

An agent harness uses each row’s data to execute a task and writes the result back into the sheet.

An agent harness reads your database schema and writes SQL queries to power dashboard charts.

An agent harness turns your brief into a shot plan and calls video tools to generate clips for the timeline.

A recruiter harness interviews you and installs each teammate as a harness of its own; teammates work together in groups, hand each other files and @mentions, and leave what they make in a shared library.

Setup notes & licensing

Start: Open Shop in the Console, pick a kit, and select a harness and model supported by your connected providers.

Dashboards: use a reachable database and a read-only database account. Set 

HR_SECRET_KEY
to encrypt stored connections, and review the sample-row setting before connecting.

Licensing: Starter Kits use different terms from Community Edition.

  • Your infrastructure. One Docker deployment for the Console, Gateway, and Runner.
  • Your credentials and state. Provider keys, sessions, files, and workspaces stay under your control. Model requests still go to your configured provider.
  • Real workspaces. Native filesystem, shell, and Git workflows, with separate session workspaces.
  • No Console product analytics. Community Edition disables the Console analytics pipeline.

Choose HarnessRouter Cloud for managed deployment, maintenance, and scaling, with tasks running in serverless, isolated sandboxes through the same API contract.

Local → Cloud Start directly in Cloud
Bring a custom harness you’ve configured locally.
Follow the upload guide →		 Create and run harnesses without a local deployment.
Open HarnessRouter Cloud →

For local uploads: set 

HR_SECRET_KEY
on your local instance to encrypt the saved destination key. Save your custom harness in Settings, select Upload to Cloud, then connect a destination using its Cloud workspace API key.

Uploads copy harness configuration, not provider keys, sessions, or generated files. Uploading again replaces that destination’s hosted copy.

      
┌─ HarnessRouter container ─────────────────────────────────┐
│  Console :3000   ← only published port                    │
│       │ same-origin proxy                                 │
│       ▼                                                   │
│  Gateway :8080   Responses API + harness lifecycle        │
│       │ loopback                                          │
│       ▼                                                   │
│  Runner  :8081   runs harnesses in session workspaces     │
│                                                           │
│  /data volume   database · files · secrets · workspaces   │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

The Gateway and Runner listen on loopback inside the container. Sessions use separate workspaces and operating-system users, not separate containers. The Console is the entry point for both UI and API.

See configuration, upgrades and backups, and public deployment with TLS.

Unified Harness Protocol (UHP) is the public, versioned contract implemented by Community Edition and HarnessRouter Cloud. Its task surface is deliberately compatible with the OpenAI Responses API, so existing Responses SDKs, streaming parsers, and UI components can work with a UHP server. UHP defines harness execution semantics for harness selection, persistent sessions, files, cancellation, and harness-managed tools and skills.

This repository contains the Apache 2.0 reference implementation, machine-readable schemas, and the conformance suite.

Once your harness runs successfully in the Console:

1. Open **API Keys** in the Console rail of the same CE instance ([default local address](http://localhost:3000/keys)), name the key, and press **Create**.
2. Store the secret shown once as `HARNESSROUTER_API_KEY` in your product backend. Never expose it in browser code. This CE-issued key is separate from your Console password and provider key.
3. Call the API with the Harness ID shown in the Console and a model served by your connected provider.

```
export HARNESSROUTER_BASE_URL=http://localhost:3000/api/harness
curl --fail-with-body -sS "$HARNESSROUTER_BASE_URL/v1/responses" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${HARNESSROUTER_API_KEY:?}" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \

    "input":"Reply with exactly: it works.",
    "metadata":{"harness_id":"codex"},

    "stream":false
```

**Join a caller's trace to the task.**

Send the W3C Trace Context headers `traceparent` and `tracestate` on the request, and the task's model calls carry a child of that trace: the same trace id, a new span id and the sampled flag, so the provider's log and yours are one trace. A value that is not valid W3C syntax is dropped, never refused: a broken tracing header does not fail a task. `baggage` is never read and never leaves the instance.

**Retry a task without running it twice.**

Send the same request with the same `Idempotency-Key` when retrying a task. For example, send this request twice using the URL and API key above (key generation needs Python 3):

```
IDEMPOTENCY_KEY=$(python3 -c 'import uuid; print(uuid.uuid4())')
for attempt in 1 2; do
  curl --fail-with-body -sS "$HARNESSROUTER_BASE_URL/v1/responses" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer ${HARNESSROUTER_API_KEY:?}" \
    -H 'content-type: application/json' \
    -H "Idempotency-Key: $IDEMPOTENCY_KEY" \
    -d '{
      "input":"Reply with exactly: it works.",
      "metadata":{"harness_id":"codex"},
      "model":"gpt-5.4-mini",
      "stream":false
    }'
  printf '\n'
done
```
Both responses have the same `id`, and the session contains one turn: the retry returns the first request's result without starting another execution. If the first request is still running, the retry waits for it. Use a new key for each new logical request. Reusing a key with a different request body returns `409`; changing only `stream` still counts as the same request. See [Tasks §6: Idempotency](/HarnessRouter/harnessrouter/blob/main/protocol/versions/2026-10-19/tasks.md#6-idempotency).

Never put a long exact value such as a token, an id or a hash in the prompt: the agent retypes what it reads, and a model drops and swaps characters in strings like that. Attach it as a file (`POST /v1/files`, then an `input_file` block; the file lands in the agent's working directory under its filename before every turn that carries it) or hand it to the agent through the harness's environment. A harness takes an `env` map whose values resolve on every turn: `$headers.X-Name` takes that header from the request (declare it in `additional_headers`), `vault:name` takes a stored secret, anything else is used as written. The agent's shell and tools start with those variables set, so a task can say "the token is in $DEPLOY\_TOKEN", and a value that came through a reference is redacted from everything that leaves the sandbox, the response, the stream, the trace and the stored record, even when the agent prints it. A `vault:` reference reads only a secret your own workspace stored through `PUT /v1/mcp-secrets/{ref}`. The redaction protects the record, not the agent: a value the agent can read it can also send elsewhere if a prompt or a page tells it to, so hand it a token scoped to the user and the task, short-lived and least privilege.

The whole API is described at `$HARNESSROUTER_BASE_URL/v1/openapi.json`, generated from the routes, with a browsable copy at `/v1/docs`.

html_zh:
代理线束的统一接口。

无需处理线束工程即可构建代理产品。 HarnessRouter 是一种基础设施层，可将 Codex 和 Claude Code 等现有工具转变为即插即用代理后端，让您的产品通过一个 API 运行任务、检索结果和切换工具。

HarnessRouter 实现统一线束协议 (UHP)并提供兼容 OpenAI 响应的 API，处理持久会话、流式传输进度、文件、工件、取消和结构化故障。

同一任务的八种线束×模型配置。每个指标都会比较其最佳和最差结果。成本最低和最快的配置因任务而异。方法论

目前有 26 个线束基地：Codex、Claude Code、Hermes、Pi、DeepSeek Harness、OpenCode、Kilo Code、Qwen Code、Gemini CLI、Cline、Oh My Pi、goose、Kimi Code CLI、MiniMax Code、Aider、OpenHands、CheetahClaws、Grok Build、Agent Zero、System One、Qoder Cloud Agent、MiMo Code、jcode、OpenSquilla、nanobot 和 ZeroClaw。支持矩阵显示哪个运行在哪个提供商上。

提示

开始使用：本地运行·集成到您的产品中·入门套件·使用托管云

在您控制的基础设施上使用您自己的提供商密钥自行托管社区版。

从一个 Docker 命令开始，等待第一次启动，然后连接模型提供程序并运行您的第一个任务。

您需要： Docker · 大约 4 GB 磁盘 · 提供商 API 密钥

无需 HarnessRouter 帐户。没有捆绑模型或试用密钥。

docker run -d --name harnessrouter \
  -p 127.0.0.1:3000:3000 \
  -v harnessrouter:/data \
  harnessrouter/harnessrouter

如果需要，Docker 会拉取镜像。命名卷会在重新启动之间保留您的数据库、文件、已安装的线束 CLI 和工作区。

现有安装或自定义设置

已经安装了吗？

docker pull harnessrouter/harnessrouter
下载最新的镜像，但不升级正在运行的容器。遵循升级备份指导.

3000端口繁忙？使用

-p 127.0.0.1:3100:3000
并打开端口 3100。使用初始凭据时保留环回绑定。

请勿添加

--user
。入口点和 Runner 需要 root 来管理每个会话的用户。控制台和网关以非特权方式运行；代理进程以其会话的用户身份运行。

有关版本固定、Compose 和脚本化设置的信息，请参阅设置指南。

docker logs -f harnessrouter

第一次启动会安装已启用的线束 CLI。当日志显示时继续：

      
[harnessrouter] ready on :3000

按 Ctrl+C 停止跟踪日志。容器继续运行。

控制台未准备好或线束丢失？

如果浏览器拒绝连接，请在控制台完成启动后几秒钟后重试。对于丢失的线束，请检查

backends available:
和任何
requested but not installed
日志中的警告。

打开http://localhost:3000或您选择的主机端口，然后登录：

用户名 
线束路由器
密码 
线束路由器

警告

更改“个人资料”中的默认密码。将实例保留在本地，直到您更改它。短暂保存会重新启动控制台并注销其他浏览器。

查看登录屏幕

使用现有卷或自定义凭据？检查凭证优先级和设置。

这些凭据使您登录到控制台。您不需要 HarnessRouter API 密钥即可在此处运行任务。

打开导轨底部的帐户菜单，然后选择自带密钥。找到您的提供商，按添加键，然后粘贴其 API 密钥。其支持的模型在控制台中可用。

该提供者密钥授权模型请求。它与下面用于产品集成的 HarnessRouter API 密钥是分开的。

查看提供商设置屏幕

打开“开始”，说出您的代理应该为您的用户做什么，然后按“继续”。在设置代理线束中，将代理线束和模型保留为“自动”或选择它们，然后保存。 HarnessRouter 在您自己的模型之一上构建设置：它编写代理指令，选择工作所需的线束、模型、技能、插件和工具，并在框中留下示例请求。发送它来运行第一个任务。

首先尝试一个例子。在 HarnessRouter 中的“开始”下，选择三个示例作业之一。它的请求会回放记录的运行，因此您无需花费令牌即可看到已完成的任务。在它下面写下以继续您自己的模型。

在 Studio 中打开设置并选择“设置”来更改其模型、说明、技能、插件、工具、环境和限制。在附加组件下为整个工作区添加插件、技能、MCP 服务器和环境。保存设置后，代理线束就会固定：进行新设置以使用另一个设置。

请参阅新设置

使用内置或自定义线束作为可插入代理后端运行产品任务。调用您的自托管实例的 OpenAI Responses 兼容 API 并选择带有

metadata.harness_id
。无需云部署。

一旦您的线束在控制台中成功运行：

  • 在同一 CE 实例的控制台栏中打开 API 密钥（默认本地地址），为密钥命名，然后按“创建”。
  • 将显示的秘密存储为
    HARNESSROUTER_API_KEY
    在您的产品后端。切勿在浏览器代码中公开它。此 CE 颁发的密钥与您的控制台密码和提供商密钥是分开的。
  • 使用控制台中显示的 Harness ID 和连接的提供商提供的模型来调用 API。
export HARNESSROUTER_BASE_URL=http://localhost:3000/api/harness

curl --fail-with-body -sS "$HARNESSROUTER_BASE_URL/v1/responses" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${HARNESSROUTER_API_KEY:?}" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "input":"Reply with exactly: it works.",
    "metadata":{"harness_id":"codex"},
    "model":"gpt-5.4-mini",
    "stream":false
  }'

任务及其副本显示在控制台的同一工作区中。放

"stream": true
接收服务器发送的事件。

将调用者的跟踪加入到任务中。

发送 W3C 跟踪上下文标头

traceparent
和
tracestate
请求上，任务的模型调用携带该跟踪的子级：相同的跟踪 id、新的跨度 id 和采样标志，​​因此提供者的日志和您的日志是同一个跟踪。无效 W3C 语法的值将被删除，而不会被拒绝：损坏的跟踪标头不会使任务失败。
baggage
永远不会被读取，也永远不会离开实例。

重试任务而不运行两次。

使用相同的内容发送相同的请求

Idempotency-Key
重试任务时。例如，使用上面的 URL 和 API 密钥发送此请求两次（密钥生成需要 Python 3）：

IDEMPOTENCY_KEY=$(python3 -c 'import uuid; print(uuid.uuid4())')

for attempt in 1 2; do
  curl --fail-with-body -sS "$HARNESSROUTER_BASE_URL/v1/responses" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer ${HARNESSROUTER_API_KEY:?}" \
    -H 'content-type: application/json' \
    -H "Idempotency-Key: $IDEMPOTENCY_KEY" \
    -d '{
      "input":"Reply with exactly: it works.",
      "metadata":{"harness_id":"codex"},
      "model":"gpt-5.4-mini",
      "stream":false
    }'
  printf '\n'
done

两个响应具有相同的

id
，并且会话包含一个回合：重试返回第一个请求的结果，而不开始另一次执行。如果第一个请求仍在运行，则重试会等待它。对每个新的逻辑请求使用新的密钥。重用具有不同请求正文的密钥会返回
409
;仅改变
stream
仍然算作同一个请求。看任务 §6：幂等性.

切勿在提示中输入长的精确值，例如令牌、ID 或哈希：代理会重新输入其读取的内容，并且模型会删除并交换字符串中的字符。将其作为文件附加（

POST /v1/files
，然后一个
input_file
堵塞;文件在每次携带该文件之前都会以其文件名降落在代理的工作目录中）或通过线束的环境将其交给代理。安全带需要一个
env
其值每回合都会解析的地图：
$headers.X-Name
从请求中获取该标头（在中声明它）
additional_headers
), 
vault:name
需要一个存储的秘密，其他任何内容都按书面使用。代理的 shell 和工具从这些变量集开始，因此任务可以说“令牌位于 $DEPLOY_TOKEN 中”，并且通过引用传入的值将从离开沙箱、响应、流、跟踪和存储记录的所有内容中进行编辑，即使代理打印它也是如此。一个
vault:
引用仅读取您自己的工作区存储的秘密
PUT /v1/mcp-secrets/{ref}
。修订保护的是记录，而不是代理：代理可以读取的值，如果提示或页面告诉它，它也可以发送到其他地方，因此将一个范围仅限于用户和任务的令牌交给它，这是短暂的且权限最小的。

整个 API 的描述位于

$HARNESSROUTER_BASE_URL/v1/openapi.json
，从路线生成，可浏览的副本位于
/v1/docs
.

当您的后端和 CE 在同一台计算机上运行时，默认 URL 有效。从另一台计算机或容器，使用 CE 实例的可访问 URL。阅读完整的自托管 API 和网络指南 →

启动任务 发送指令并检查执行状态
继续会议 发送后续指令
先前的响应 ID
串流进度 在代理工作时接收实时更新
处理文件 附加输入文件并检索生成的输出
取消任务 停止不再需要的工作
检查执行情况 检查结构化错误和执行跟踪

通过代理工具增强产品中的代理功能，包括创建内容和分析数据等知识工作任务。探索这些即用型套件，了解作为可插拔后端的线束的实际应用情况。

代理工具可将您的简介转变为可编辑幻灯片的幻灯片内容和布局。

代理工具使用每行的数据来执行任务并将结果写回到工作表中。

代理工具读取您的数据库架构并写入 SQL 查询来支持仪表板图表。

代理工具将您的简报转化为拍摄计划，并调用视频工具为时间线生成剪辑。

招聘人员会面试你，并将每个队友安装为自己的安全带；团队成员以小组形式一起工作，互相传递文件和@提及，并将他们制作的内容留在共享库中。

设置说明和许可

开始：在控制台中打开商店，选择一个套件，然后选择您所连接的提供商支持的线束和型号。

仪表板：使用可访问的数据库和只读数据库帐户。放

HR_SECRET_KEY
加密存储的连接，并在连接之前检查示例行设置。

许可：入门套件使用与社区版不同的术语。

  • 您的基础设施。控制台、网关和运行器的一个 Docker 部署。
  • 您的凭据和状态。提供程序密钥、会话、文件和工作区均在您的控制之下。模型请求仍会发送至您配置的提供程序。
  • 真实的工作空间。本机文件系统、shell 和 Git 工作流程，具有单独的会话工作区。
  • 没有控制台产品分析。社区版禁用控制台分析管道。

选择 HarnessRouter Cloud 进行托管部署、维护和扩展，任务通过相同的 API 合约在无服务器、隔离的沙箱中运行。

本地 → 云端 直接在云端启动
带上您在本地配置的自定义线束。
按照上传指南→		 创建并运行线束，无需本地部署。
打开 HarnessRouter 云 →

对于本地上传：设置

HR_SECRET_KEY
在您的本地实例上加密保存的目标密钥。在“设置”中保存自定义线束，选择“上传到云”，然后使用其云工作区 API 密钥连接目标。

上传复制工具配置，而不是提供程序密钥、会话或生成的文件。再次上传会替换该目标的托管副本。

      
┌─ HarnessRouter container ─────────────────────────────────┐
│  Console :3000   ← only published port                    │
│       │ same-origin proxy                                 │
│       ▼                                                   │
│  Gateway :8080   Responses API + harness lifecycle        │
│       │ loopback                                          │
│       ▼                                                   │
│  Runner  :8081   runs harnesses in session workspaces     │
│                                                           │
│  /data volume   database · files · secrets · workspaces   │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Gateway 和 Runner 监听容器内的环回。会话使用单独的工作区和操作系统用户，而不是单独的容器。控制台是 UI 和 API 的入口点。

请参阅配置、 升级和备份以及使用 TLS 的公共部署。

统一线束协议 (UHP)是由 Community Edition 和 HarnessRouter Cloud 实施的公共版本化合同。其任务界面特意与 OpenAI Responses API 兼容，因此现有的 Responses SDK、流解析器和 UI 组件可以与 UHP 服务器配合使用。 UHP 定义了用于线束选择、持久会话、文件、取消以及线束管理工具和技能的线束执行语义。

该存储库包含 Apache 2.0 参考实现、机器可读模式和一致性套件。

summary_zh: HarnessRouter 社区版是一个自托管的基础设施层，把 Codex、Claude Code 等现成 Agent Harness 变成即插即用的后端。它实现了统一协议 UHP，并提供兼容 OpenAI Responses 的 API，负责持久会话、流式进度、文件与产物、取消和结构化错误。目前支持 26 种 Harness，包括 Codex、Claude Code、Hermes、Pi、OpenCode、Gemini CLI、Cline、Aider、OpenHands 和 Grok Build 等。项目还给出了同一任务下不同 Harness 与模型组合的成本和速度对比。
